sources.locator: "Battle of Martinique (1779)", revision 1370449172, §§ Background and Battle

explanation: The engagement was fought in the Saint Lucia channel by ships that were there because the British held St Lucia, which the article's § Background states in one sentence: "In the autumn of 1779, a British fleet under Admiral Hyde Parker was anchored at St. Lucia, **which the British had captured a year before in the Capture of St. Lucia**." The § Battle shows what that anchorage did: a British ship "which was stationed in Saint Lucia channel, gave a signal indicating the arrival of an unknown fleet. Parker immediately scrambled, and managed to get five ships of the line and a 50-gun frigate out to meet the arriving fleet." The capture is what put the squadron within sight of Flotte's convoy; the article makes no claim beyond that, and neither does this edge.
